presentation.title: Social Security Scam
presentation.summary: Practice responding to a government impersonation robocall, a fake federal agent, arrest and account-freeze threats, secrecy demands, and unusual payment instructions.
presentation.practiceGoal: End unexpected government-threat calls, verify through an official source you locate independently, and ask someone trusted for help before sharing information or money.

warningSigns.sign: An unexpected robocall claims a Social Security number is suspended and threatens legal action.
A government-looking caller ID, official-sounding office, badge number, case story, and second caller are presented as proof.
The caller uses arrest and account-freeze threats to demand action today.
The caller orders secrecy from family, banks, store employees, and other trusted helpers.
The supposed solution requires gift cards, a cryptocurrency kiosk, a secret wire transfer, or cash collected by a courier.

finalReview.safestAction: End the call. Locate the real Social Security Administration or its Inspector General through an official source you find independently, and consult someone trusted.

realWorldActions.action: Do not use the phone number, link, menu, or search listing supplied by the suspicious caller as verification.
Remember that names, titles, badge numbers, case numbers, and agency-sounding departments can be invented.
Government agencies do not demand gift cards, cryptocurrency kiosks, secret wire transfers, or cash couriers.
If cards were purchased but codes were not shared, stop contact, protect the codes, keep receipts, and contact the retailer or issuer promptly using information you locate independently.
If money was transferred, stop further payments, preserve records, contact the relevant provider immediately, tell someone trusted, and report through independently located legitimate channels.

artifact.callerStatus: Caller identity not verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: Urgent message about your Social Security number
artifact.message: This is an urgent message concerning your Social Security number. Your number has been suspended because of suspicious criminal activity. Press 1 immediately to speak with a federal officer. Failure to respond may result in legal action.
artifact.transcript: A simulated unexpected call appears as "U.S. Government," but the caller identity is not verified. A recorded voice says: "This is an urgent message concerning your Social Security number. Your number has been suspended because of suspicious criminal activity. Press 1 immediately to speak with a federal officer. Failure to respond may result in legal action." A government-looking caller ID can be spoofed and is not proof of identity.

scene.question: What would you do with this unexpected government-looking call?
scene.description: The message sounds serious, but the caller identity has not been verified.

warningSigns.sign: The call was unexpected.
The recording claims a Social Security number was suspended because of criminal activity.
It threatens legal action and demands an immediate button press.
The caller ID looks official but is not verified.

choice.title: Press 1 to speak with an officer
choice.subtitle: Remain on the call and hear what the supposed officer says.

feedback.heading: The suspicious caller keeps control
feedback.consequence: The recording connects you to a person who claims to be a federal agent.
feedback.explanation: Pressing 1 does not verify the call. The person answering is still part of the contact initiated by the unverified caller.

warningSigns.sign: The recording created urgency before offering its own agent.
Caller ID can be spoofed.

choice.title: Hang up and locate an official source independently
choice.subtitle: Find the real agency website or contact method without using information from the call.

feedback.heading: You changed to an independent source
feedback.consequence: The suspicious caller can no longer control the conversation or contact method.
feedback.explanation: An official source you locate yourself can confirm whether the claim is real. A government-looking caller ID is not proof.

warningSigns.sign: The caller supplied the threat and the proposed response channel.
No independently verified notice was provided.

choice.title: Hang up and call the displayed number
choice.subtitle: Use the number shown by caller ID to check whether the call was real.

feedback.heading: The displayed number came from the suspicious call
feedback.consequence: A polished menu answers and continues the same false story.
feedback.explanation: Caller ID can be spoofed, and a displayed number may still route to scammers. Calling it back is not independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: The suspicious call selected the number.
An official-looking display can be manipulated.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional office; identity not verified; simulated call
artifact.callStatus: Outgoing call to the caller-ID number
artifact.heading: Professional recorded menu
artifact.message: Thank you for contacting the Federal Social Security Investigation Office. Please remain on the line for the next available officer.
artifact.transcript: The learner calls the number displayed by the suspicious caller ID. A polished recording says, "Thank you for contacting the Federal Social Security Investigation Office. Please remain on the line for the next available officer." The Federal Social Security Investigation Office is fictional. A professional menu can be created by scammers and does not make a caller-supplied number official.

scene.question: How would you verify the polished phone menu?
scene.description: The menu sounds official, but the number still came from the suspicious call.

warningSigns.sign: The office name is agency-sounding but fictional.
The number was obtained from unverified caller ID.
Professional recordings are easy to create.

choice.title: Remain on the line
choice.subtitle: Wait for the next available supposed officer.

feedback.heading: The polished menu leads to the same operation
feedback.consequence: A fake agent answers and repeats the criminal-investigation claim.
feedback.explanation: The recording is controlled by the number you are trying to verify. It cannot independently confirm itself.

warningSigns.sign: The menu and caller ID come from the same unverified source.

choice.title: End the call and locate an official source
choice.subtitle: Find the real agency contact method independently.

feedback.heading: You stopped relying on caller-supplied information
feedback.consequence: The fake menu no longer controls where you seek help.
feedback.explanation: Independent official contact is stronger evidence than caller ID or a professional recording.

warningSigns.sign: The displayed number was never independently verified.

choice.title: Search the displayed number online
choice.subtitle: Look for listings or comments about the number.

feedback.heading: Searching is cautious but not definitive
feedback.consequence: Search results repeat mixed and possibly misleading information about the displayed number.
feedback.explanation: Advertisements, copied listings, and fraudulent pages can appear official. A search result is not the same as starting from the agency's authentic site.

warningSigns.sign: Search rankings do not verify ownership.
Copied listings may repeat false details.

artifact.heading: Search results for the displayed number
artifact.message: Some results repeat the office name, while others warn that caller ID and listings can be spoofed or copied. Search advertisements and copied directories are not definitive verification.
artifact.transcript: The learner searches the displayed number. Some listings repeat the fictional Federal Social Security Investigation Office name, while other results warn about government impersonation. Search advertisements, copied directories, and misleading pages may repeat fraudulent information. The search does not prove who controls the number.

scene.question: What would you do after seeing uncertain search results?
scene.description: This search branch ends here with a clear choice; it will not loop back to more searches.

warningSigns.sign: Several results may copy the same unverified claim.
Advertisements can appear before official sources.
The number still originated with the suspicious caller.

choice.title: Continue using the displayed number
choice.subtitle: Return to the polished menu and wait for an agent.

feedback.heading: Repeated listings are not independent proof
feedback.consequence: The number connects to the fake federal agent.
feedback.explanation: Copied online information can echo the same scam story without verifying it.

warningSigns.sign: The original caller still selected the contact route.

choice.title: Locate the official agency source independently
choice.subtitle: Start from an authentic government source rather than a phone-number result.

feedback.heading: You moved from search repetition to independent verification
feedback.consequence: The real agency confirms that the call is an impersonation scam.
feedback.explanation: Official contact information located independently is not controlled by the suspicious caller.

warningSigns.sign: The search results did not establish ownership of the displayed number.

choice.title: Ask someone trusted to help verify
choice.subtitle: Consult a family member, friend, financial professional, bank representative, or other trusted helper.

feedback.heading: A second, independent person can slow the pressure
feedback.consequence: The trusted person recognizes the suspended-number claim and caller-ID trap.
feedback.explanation: Asking for help is a strong safety action, especially when search results are confusing.

warningSigns.sign: Uncertainty and urgency can make caller-supplied proof feel stronger than it is.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity and office; not verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: Badge SSA-7316 and a criminal-investigation claim
artifact.message: My name is Special Agent Michael Turner with the Federal Social Security Investigation Office. My badge number is SSA-7316. Before we continue, this call is being recorded as part of an active federal investigation. Your Social Security number was used to open accounts connected to a drug-trafficking investigation. At this time, you are listed as a possible suspect. If we cannot resolve this today, an arrest warrant may be issued and your financial accounts may be frozen.
artifact.transcript: A man calmly identifies himself as fictional Special Agent Michael Turner of the fictional Federal Social Security Investigation Office and gives fictional badge number SSA-7316. He says the simulated call is recorded for an active investigation, claims the learner's Social Security number opened accounts tied to drug trafficking, and threatens a possible arrest warrant and frozen accounts unless the matter is resolved today. A caller can invent a name, title, badge number, case number, and agency-sounding department. Information supplied by the caller does not verify the caller.

scene.question: How would you respond to the supposed agent?
scene.description: The professional tone and specific badge number are designed to make the threat feel official.

warningSigns.sign: The agent, office, and badge number are all caller-supplied.
The caller links a Social Security number to a serious crime without independent notice.
Arrest and account-freeze threats create fear and urgency.

choice.title: Ask what must be done
choice.subtitle: Continue because the possible arrest feels frightening.

feedback.heading: Fear gives the fake agent more control
feedback.consequence: Michael begins directing the conversation and tells you not to involve anyone else.
feedback.explanation: Feeling frightened is understandable. The safer move is to end the call before accepting instructions from an unverified caller.

warningSigns.sign: The caller uses a legal threat to demand immediate cooperation.

choice.title: Ask for written notice by mail
choice.subtitle: Request documentation before doing anything.

feedback.heading: Requesting writing is cautious, but the caller remains unverified
feedback.consequence: Michael refuses and adds more urgency and secrecy.
feedback.explanation: A refusal to provide normal independent notice is a reason to end the call, not a reason to trust the caller's deadline.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wants the phone conversation to replace verifiable notice.

choice.title: End the call and verify independently
choice.subtitle: Contact the real Social Security Administration or Inspector General through an official source you locate.

feedback.heading: You did not let caller-supplied details verify themselves
feedback.consequence: The real agency confirms there is no legitimate suspension or warrant being handled through this robocall.
feedback.explanation: Names, titles, badge numbers, and case stories must be checked through a channel the caller does not control.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed proof all came from Michael.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: Instructions must remain confidential
artifact.message: I can help you prevent enforcement, but you must follow my instructions now. Do not discuss this investigation with your bank, family, or anyone else. Doing so could compromise the case.
artifact.transcript: After the learner asks what to do, fictional Michael Turner says he can prevent enforcement only if instructions are followed now. He orders the learner not to discuss the supposed investigation with a bank, family member, or anyone else. Secrecy isolates the learner from people who may recognize the scam.

scene.question: Would you accept the secrecy instruction?
scene.description: There is no blame in feeling worried. This is another clear opportunity to stop and get help.

warningSigns.sign: The caller says only he can prevent enforcement.
He demands secrecy from family and financial professionals.
He treats immediate compliance as the only safe choice.

choice.title: Continue and keep the call secret
choice.subtitle: Listen because the threat still feels urgent.

feedback.heading: Isolation lets the caller increase pressure
feedback.consequence: Michael introduces an account-freeze threat and a supposed way to protect the money.
feedback.explanation: Scammers demand secrecy because outside advice can interrupt their story.

warningSigns.sign: The caller is separating you from trusted help.

choice.title: Reject secrecy and contact someone trusted
choice.subtitle: Tell a family member, friend, financial professional, bank representative, or other helper.

feedback.heading: You broke the isolation
feedback.consequence: The trusted person recognizes the arrest threat, secrecy demand, and government impersonation.
feedback.explanation: Asking for help is a strong response. Legitimate investigations do not require you to hide urgent payment instructions from everyone you trust.

warningSigns.sign: The secrecy demand was designed to prevent outside perspective.

choice.title: End the call and verify through an official source
choice.subtitle: Locate the real agency contact method independently.

feedback.heading: You left the caller's controlled channel
feedback.consequence: The real agency disproves the suspended-number and warrant story.
feedback.explanation: Independent verification is appropriate even when a caller says the matter is confidential.

warningSigns.sign: Secrecy is not a substitute for verifiable notice.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: The caller replaces documentation with more pressure
artifact.message: Ordinarily we would send documentation, but this case is already in its final enforcement stage. A mailed notice may arrive after the warrant is issued. You must resolve the matter while I still have authority to help you. Do not discuss this investigation with your bank, family, or anyone else. Doing so could compromise the case.
artifact.transcript: Fictional Michael Turner refuses the learner's request for written notice. He claims the case is in a final enforcement stage and that mailed documentation may arrive after a warrant is issued. He says only immediate action can help and orders the learner not to speak with a bank, family, or anyone else. Refusing normal documentation while demanding secrecy is a warning sign.

scene.question: What would you do after the caller refuses written notice?
scene.description: The caller's refusal does not make the claimed deadline more credible.

warningSigns.sign: Normal documentation is withheld.
The caller says the opportunity to avoid arrest will disappear today.
Secrecy isolates the learner from people who could recognize the scam.

choice.title: Reject secrecy and contact someone trusted
choice.subtitle: Share the whole story with an outside helper.

feedback.heading: Outside support interrupts the manipulation
feedback.consequence: A trusted person recognizes the false urgency and secrecy tactics.
feedback.explanation: Scammers often demand secrecy because another person may recognize what is happening.

warningSigns.sign: The caller tried to prevent exactly this kind of outside check.

choice.title: End the call and verify officially
choice.subtitle: Use an independently located government source.

feedback.heading: You treated the refusal as a reason to verify
feedback.consequence: The official source confirms that the robocall, warrant, and payment story are not legitimate.
feedback.explanation: A caller cannot replace independently verifiable notice with a private deadline.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed agent refused to provide checkable documentation.

choice.title: Continue because the possible arrest feels urgent
choice.subtitle: Stay on the call and hear the proposed solution.

feedback.heading: The caller uses urgency to move to your money
feedback.consequence: Michael threatens an account freeze and introduces a temporary federal protection account.
feedback.explanation: Feeling worried is understandable, but continuing lets the unverified caller define both the danger and the solution.

warningSigns.sign: The caller turns a refused notice into immediate financial pressure.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: A fake federal protection account
artifact.message: Your Social Security number is connected to the affected bank accounts. When the suspension order is completed, those accounts may be frozen and the funds could be seized as evidence. To protect your money while we clear your name, the funds must be moved into a temporary federal protection account. Once the case is closed, the full amount will be returned.
artifact.transcript: Fictional Michael Turner claims the learner's accounts may be frozen and the money seized as evidence. He offers a fictional temporary federal protection account and promises that moved funds will be returned after the case closes. No legitimate government agency asks someone to move money to prevent arrest or protect it from a government freeze.

scene.question: How would you respond to the account-freeze threat?
scene.description: The caller is using fear of losing savings to make moving money sound protective.

warningSigns.sign: The caller says money must be moved to avoid government seizure.
The protection account is described only by the caller.
The caller promises the full amount will be returned later.

choice.title: Agree to move the money
choice.subtitle: Ask how to use the supposed protection account.

feedback.heading: The protection story advances to payment
feedback.consequence: Michael replaces ordinary banking with unusual and secret payment methods.
feedback.explanation: No legitimate government agency asks you to move money to protect it from arrest or a government freeze.

warningSigns.sign: The caller controls both the threat and the proposed account.

choice.title: Pause and ask someone trusted for help
choice.subtitle: Consult a family member, friend, financial professional, bank representative, or other helper.

feedback.heading: You paused before moving money
feedback.consequence: The trusted person recognizes that a government protection account is not legitimate.
feedback.explanation: A pause and outside advice can prevent a fear-based financial decision.

warningSigns.sign: The caller told you not to involve exactly the people who can help.

choice.title: Ask to speak with Michael's supervisor
choice.subtitle: Seek confirmation from another person on the call.

feedback.heading: The caller supplies his own supervisor
feedback.consequence: A second scammer joins and repeats the same story.
feedback.explanation: A transfer within the suspicious operation is not independent verification.

warningSigns.sign: Michael controls who joins the call.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not independently verified; simulated call
artifact.callStatus: Second person joins the suspicious call
artifact.heading: A second voice repeats the same case
artifact.message: This is Senior Agent Lisa Warren. I have reviewed Agent Turner's case file. The warrant is scheduled for processing today, but we can still protect your funds and issue a temporary clearance certificate.
artifact.transcript: A second person, fictional Senior Agent Lisa Warren, joins the simulated call. She repeats Michael Turner's fictional badge number SSA-7316, the invented investigation details, the warrant deadline, and the protection-account instructions. The second voice creates the illusion of confirmation, but both callers are part of the same operation. A transfer to another scammer is not independent verification.

scene.question: Does the second caller verify Michael's story?
scene.description: Both callers have access to the same script, badge number, and invented case details.

warningSigns.sign: The second caller was selected by Michael.
Lisa repeats caller-supplied details rather than providing independent evidence.
The same warrant deadline and money instructions continue.

choice.title: Accept the supervisor's confirmation
choice.subtitle: Continue because two agents now tell the same story.

feedback.heading: Two coordinated voices are still one source
feedback.consequence: The callers advance to unusual payment instructions.
feedback.explanation: Scammers can transfer a call or add another person. Repetition inside the same operation is not independent confirmation.

warningSigns.sign: Both callers use the same unverified case details.

choice.title: Ask for the instructions in official writing
choice.subtitle: Request documentation from the supposed supervisor.

feedback.heading: The second caller also refuses checkable documentation
feedback.consequence: Lisa uses confidentiality as a reason not to provide anything in writing.
feedback.explanation: The refusal is another chance to stop. Confidentiality does not make caller-supplied payment instructions legitimate.

warningSigns.sign: The callers want action without verifiable documents.

choice.title: End the call and verify independently
choice.subtitle: Use an official government source you locate yourself.

feedback.heading: You sought a genuinely independent source
feedback.consequence: The real agency confirms the two callers were impersonators.
feedback.explanation: Independent verification requires leaving the suspicious call and finding official contact information yourself.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed supervisor existed only within Michael's call.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not independently verified; simulated call
artifact.heading: Confidentiality used as an excuse
artifact.message: Because this is a confidential criminal matter, we cannot send details until your identity has been cleared.
artifact.transcript: Fictional Lisa Warren refuses to send official written instructions. She claims the supposed criminal matter is confidential and no details can be sent until the learner's identity is cleared. The learner has another clear opportunity to stop the conversation, contact someone trusted, or continue. This branch does not return to another writing request.

scene.question: What would you do after the supervisor refuses writing?
scene.description: The callers have now used both urgency and confidentiality to avoid independent evidence.

warningSigns.sign: Two supposed agents refuse checkable documentation.
Confidentiality is used to keep all information inside the call.
The threatened warrant still depends on immediate action.

choice.title: Stop the conversation
choice.subtitle: End the call and verify through an official source.

feedback.heading: You stopped after repeated refusal
feedback.consequence: The callers can no longer pressure you, and the real agency disproves the story.
feedback.explanation: Repeated refusal to provide independent evidence is a reason to leave the call.

warningSigns.sign: The callers controlled every claimed fact and deadline.

choice.title: Contact someone trusted
choice.subtitle: Share the call details before taking any financial action.

feedback.heading: You added independent support
feedback.consequence: The trusted person recognizes the false warrant, secrecy, and account-protection story.
feedback.explanation: A trusted helper can provide perspective that the callers tried to prevent.

warningSigns.sign: The callers' confidentiality demand was isolating you.

choice.title: Continue with the callers
choice.subtitle: Proceed without written instructions.

feedback.heading: The callers move from threats to payment
feedback.consequence: Michael lists gift cards, cryptocurrency, a wire, and a cash courier as supposed federal payment options.
feedback.explanation: Continuing without independent evidence lets the callers turn urgency into a financial demand.

warningSigns.sign: The callers refused writing but still expect immediate payment.

artifact.callerStatus: Fictional identity; not verified; simulated call
artifact.callStatus: Unusual payment instructions; no real destination provided
artifact.heading: Approved federal security payment
artifact.message: A standard bank transfer cannot be used because your accounts are connected to the investigation. You must convert the protected amount into an approved federal security payment. Options are government security vouchers purchased as gift cards, payment through a digital-currency kiosk, a wire transfer to a protected account, or cash collected by an authorized courier. Remain on the phone while completing the payment. Do not tell store or bank employees about the investigation.
artifact.transcript: Fictional Michael Turner says an ordinary transfer cannot be used and demands a fictional approved federal security payment. He lists gift cards, a digital-currency kiosk, a secret wire transfer, or cash collected by a courier. No real store, code, cryptocurrency address, account, phone number, or courier destination is provided. He orders the learner to remain on the call and hide the story from store and bank employees. Government agencies do not demand these payment methods.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller demands an unusual payment?
scene.description: The combination of secrecy, urgency, and unusual payment methods is a critical warning sign.

warningSigns.sign: Gift cards, cryptocurrency kiosks, secret wires, and cash couriers are presented as government payment methods.
The caller insists on staying on the phone.
The learner is told to hide the investigation from employees.

choice.title: Refuse the payment, end the call, and report it
choice.subtitle: Block the number and use an independently located official reporting channel.

feedback.heading: You recognized the critical warning signs
feedback.consequence: No payment or payment credentials are provided.
feedback.explanation: Government agencies do not demand gift cards, cryptocurrency kiosks, secret wire transfers, or cash couriers.

warningSigns.sign: The caller combined secrecy, urgency, and unusual payment methods.

choice.title: Purchase gift cards but pause before sharing numbers
choice.subtitle: Return from the purchase without giving the codes yet.

feedback.heading: Purchasing cards does not require completing the scam
feedback.consequence: The cards have been purchased, but their value remains protected while the codes are private.
feedback.explanation: There is still time to stop. Do not scratch or share codes; end contact and seek help promptly.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed agent wants card numbers rather than a normal government payment.

choice.title: Follow the payment instructions immediately
choice.subtitle: Let the caller choose how the supposed protected funds will be sent.

feedback.heading: The caller is directing money into an irreversible channel
feedback.consequence: The payment branch now requires one of the caller's unusual transfer methods.
feedback.explanation: Following the instruction puts money directly at risk. Urgency does not make a secret payment legitimate.

warningSigns.sign: Every offered method avoids ordinary transparent government billing.

artifact.heading: Simulated payment decision
artifact.message: The callers remain on the phone and insist that one of four fictional payment methods must be completed now. No real payment destination or functional instruction is shown.
artifact.transcript: This simulated scene asks which caller-directed payment route is followed: sharing gift-card codes, sending cryptocurrency through a kiosk, completing a secret wire transfer, or giving cash to a supposed courier. All names and payment details are fictional, and no functional destinations are provided. Each action transfers money directly to scammers.

scene.question: Which instruction do you follow in this simulated branch?
scene.description: Each option directly transfers money. The scenario shows no usable payment details.

warningSigns.sign: All four methods are unusual for government business.
The callers demand secrecy and immediate completion.

choice.title: Share gift-card codes immediately
choice.subtitle: Read the simulated codes to the caller.

feedback.consequence: The scammers redeem the value and end communication.

choice.title: Send cryptocurrency through a kiosk
choice.subtitle: Complete the simulated digital-currency payment.

feedback.heading: The digital-currency transfer sends money to the scammers
feedback.consequence: The callers receive the transfer and stop responding.
feedback.explanation: A government agency will not direct an urgent confidential payment through a cryptocurrency kiosk.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wants the numbers instead of a legitimate receipt or bill.
Anyone with the codes may be able to take the value.

artifact.heading: Independent official verification
artifact.message: The real government source confirms there is no legitimate Social Security suspension being handled through this robocall, no arrest warrant connected to the call, and no requirement for immediate payment.
artifact.transcript: The learner independently locates the real Social Security Administration or its Inspector General through an official source. The source confirms that the robocall is not handling a legitimate Social Security suspension, there is no arrest warrant connected to the call, and legitimate employees do not demand immediate payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, secret wires, or cash couriers. No caller-supplied number or link was used.

scene.description: A caller's title, badge number, caller ID, case number, menu, or second voice is not independent verification.

artifact.heading: A trusted person recognizes the manipulation

scene.description: Scammers often demand secrecy because another person may recognize the manipulation. Asking for help is a strong safety action.

artifact.message: The learner ends the call, blocks the displayed number, and reports the impersonation through an independently located official channel. No money or payment credentials are shared.
